title: Python SDK: lightweight typed-views + async fragment hydration for streaming responses
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: long-running streaming responses (chat/LLM generation + structured JSON partials) cause large memory peaks and slow parsing when we eagerly hydrate full Pydantic models per-chunk. Also, users need ergonomic, typed access to partial/late-arriving fields (e.g., metadata or usage) without waiting for stream end. Goal: design and implement 'typed views' and 'async fragments' in the Python SDK — lightweight, zero-copy view objects backed by the underlying stream buffer that allow incremental hydration of typed fields and low-overhead iteration over events. Provide clear examples, migration notes, and robust retry/idempotency semantics for fragment reassembly.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a BaseView API that exposes fields lazily and supports both dataclass and pydantic backends
Implement AsyncFragmentReader that yields typed fragments as soon as their JSON is parseable without buffering entire response
Demonstrate example patterns (chat streaming with metadata, embedding pipelines with incremental embeddings) in SDK examples and docs
Unit and integration tests showing memory usage improvement >= 2x on long-running streams (10k tokens)
Backward-compatible defaults: existing SDK behavior unchanged unless opt-in flag enabled
PR with API docs, examples and two internal library consumers migrated (console + examples)
proposal: Introduce two cooperating primitives: (1) typed 'View' objects that act as a lazy overlay on top of parsed JSON tokens. Views map keys to attribute accessors that parse on first access and cache the result. They are lightweight (no automatic deep-copy into Pydantic unless requested). (2) AsyncFragmentReader — a streaming parser that yields event fragments (complete sub-objects) as soon as they close. Each fragment is handed an associated View that allows typed field access without forcing parse of unrelated fields. The parser will support backpressure by exposing an awaitable .ack() on the fragment to signal consumption. Provide opt-in flag `streaming_typed_views=True` in client config.
design_notes:
- Use or extend existing C-optimized JSON tokenizer we have in runtime (if available) to avoid full deserialization.
- Default implementation keeps compatibility by returning the old StreamEvent objects; new views wrap StreamEvent.payload.
- Choose explicit opt-in for pydantic hydration to avoid surprising runtime costs: `fragment.hydrate(pydantic_model=MyModel)`.
- Dataclasses supported via small shim that accepts frozen dataclasses and type hints.
- For typed unions and variant fields, Views expose `get_union(tag_field)` helper to pick correct model lazily.
implementation_plan:
1) RFC PR describing API surface and migration plan (done).
2) Low-level parser: add AsyncFragmentReader in sdk/_streaming/parser.py (3 days).
3) View layer: implement BaseView + pydantic/dataclass adapters in sdk/models/views.py (4 days).
4) Add opt-in flag and example notebooks (2 days).
5) Tests & perf harness + memory regression tests (3 days).
6) Docs, migration guide, and example conversion for console streaming routes (2 days).
7) Rollout: feature-gate behind `streaming_typed_views` and add telemetry for adoption (1 day).
risks:
- Increased complexity in SDK internals leading to subtle bugs in serialization/round-trip.
- Interaction with retry semantics: if server replays fragments or partials after reconnect, we must ensure idempotent hydration. Plan: fragments carry an id + ordinal; SDK reassembly dedupes using (fragment_id, ordinal).
- Pydantic model validation during streaming could raise exceptions mid-stream; must surface as fragment-level errors rather than bubbling and closing the whole iterator. We'll attach errors to fragment objects.
tests: unit: BaseView attribute lazy parse correctness and caching
unit: dataclass and pydantic adapter parity tests
integration: end-to-end chat streaming using AsyncFragmentReader comparing memory and throughput vs baseline
fault-injection: server resends fragment N to verify dedupe and idempotency
performance: benchmark harness that measures peak memory and time-to-first-usable-fragment for 10k token stream
migrations_and_migration_notes:
- No automatic change to existing consumers. To enable: Client(session_config=..., streaming_typed_views=True).
- Migration guide will show three patterns: (1) immediate hydrate for existing code (fragment.hydrate(MyModel)), (2) gradual adoption: access only fields used and avoid full hydrate, (3) full materialization when needed: fragment.to_pydantic(MyModel).
- Example notebook migrating console streaming route `chat/stream` consumer: shows ~40% memory reduction by switching to views and only hydrating reply text until end.
review_feedback: PM (Lina Wu): request to add migration checklist and call out telemetry for opt-in adoption
Eng (Ravi Desai): suggested that fragment ack() be cancellable and propagate cancellation to upstream to free buffers earlier
Security (Nadia Green): ensure fragments don't retain references to KMS-protected plaintext; add explicit zeroization hooks for sensitive fields
DX (Jamie Ortiz): asked for ergonomic code samples that show both sync wrapper and async native usage
